Interface design should reduce review burden by highlighting only high-value discrepan cies, requiring active confirmation, and avoiding default acceptance.

For prostate MRI reporting, that principle means that the radiologist –not the model– must remain responsible for the signed clinical report and for deciding whether any generated text is clinically faithful to the images and source report.

For patient-facing explanations, institutions should disclose AI assistance when generated text is presented to patients, 1 3 Abdominal Radiology provide a pathway for questions, and define who is respon sible for review and correction.

Implementation should include a data-flow map; data minimization; role-based access controls; local or secure pro cessing where feasible; explicit limits on prompt retention, model training, and secondary use; access logs; encryption; vendor due diligence; and a breach/incident-response plan aligned with applicable law.

Continuous post-deployment monitoring should track not only model accuracy but also workflow burden, alert fatigue, patient complaints, privacy incidents, and error modes after model or template updates.
generated statements should include provenance linking them to source sen tences, structured fields, or finalized report content so that the radiologist can independently verify the output.

unlisted_practices: Enforce a strict "no new facts" rule in LLM-generated clinical text, prohibiting the model from adding, inferring, or fabricating findings or recommendations absent from the source report.
Constrain LLM outputs to a predefined schema where possible.

Do not deploy autonomous PI-RADS assignment, unsupervised staging language, or unsupervised patient counseling by general-purpose LLMs without prospective validation and clinically accountable workflow.
Place LLM after report drafting but before final sign-off, using it mainly to flag missing elements and inconsistencies, with model-suggested text shown as draft with change tracking.
Generate patient-facing explanations only after the radiology report is finalized, label them as explanations, and use centrally approved definitions.
Define before deployment who reviews and is accountable for patient-facing AI output.
